claims.text: The stability and coherence of protective oxide layers on CrFeCoNiX alloys above 900 °C are governed by the selective oxidation kinetics of X.
Al in CrFeCoNiAl forms a dense, low-thermal-expansion alpha-Al2O3 scale.
Si in CrFeCoNiSi forms SiO2 or a protective SiO2/Cr2O3 composite scale.
The oxides produced by Mn in CrFeCoNiMn are volatile or porous.
Dense Al- or Si-bearing oxide scales remain continuous and adherent during exposure above 900 °C.
Mn-bearing oxide scales are unstable and prone to cracking and spallation.
Al- or Si-containing alloys are expected to develop a dense and continuous alpha-Al2O3 or SiO2/Cr2O3 protective layer.
The Mn-containing alloy is expected to develop discontinuous or porous Mn oxide intermingled with Cr oxides.
High oxygen affinity and controlled diffusion of Al or Si promote rapid formation of low-stress, coherent oxide scales.
Mn oxidation produces volatile or porous oxides that induce local stresses, cracks, and spallation.
Oxide-scale integrity is determined by oxide density, thermal-expansion mismatch, and growth kinetics.
Under identical exposure conditions above 900 °C, Al- and Si-containing alloys will retain coherent scales while the Mn-containing alloy will exhibit discontinuous, cracked, or spalled scales.
The proposed behavior applies within compositions that retain a single-phase metallic solid solution.
Extensive phase separation or substantially different atmospheres may introduce additional oxidation phenomena.
An alloy lacking a protective oxide former, or containing minimal Al or Si, forms a nonprotective oxide and can serve as the baseline.
Failure of the Al- or Si-containing alloys to form dense coherent scales, or formation of a continuous stable scale by the Mn-containing alloy, would falsify the proposed ordering.
